text: All user accounts must enforce multi-factor authentication for access to corporate systems. Privileged accounts require hardware security tokens (FIDO2), while standard accounts may use authenticator apps. SMS-based MFA is prohibited for all account types.

Passwords must be a minimum of 14 characters for standard accounts and 20 characters for privileged accounts. Password rotation is required every 90 days for privileged accounts. Password reuse is prohibited for the last 24 passwords. Passphrases are encouraged over complex character requirements.

Security incidents must be reported to the Security Operations Center within 15 minutes of detection. The SOC will triage and classify incidents using a four-tier severity system. Critical and high severity incidents require executive notification within 1 hour and regulatory notification within 72 hours where applicable.

All corporate data must be classified into four categories: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Data owners are responsible for assigning classification labels. Restricted data requires encryption at rest and in transit, access logging, and DLP policy enforcement.

Corporate computing resources must be used for authorized business purposes only. Personal use is permitted during non-business hours provided it does not violate any other security policies. Installation of unauthorized software, cryptocurrency mining, and accessing prohibited content are strictly forbidden.

All changes to production systems must follow the formal change management process including submission, review, approval, implementation, and post-implementation verification. Emergency changes require verbal approval from the Change Advisory Board chair followed by retrospective documentation within 24 hours.

Critical systems must be backed up daily with incremental backups and weekly full backups. Backup data must be encrypted using AES-256 and replicated to a geographically separate site. Backup restoration tests must be conducted quarterly, with results documented and reported to IT management.

Remote access to corporate resources is permitted only through the approved VPN solution with MFA enforcement. Split tunneling is disabled by default. Remote access sessions are limited to 12 hours and require re-authentication. Endpoint compliance checks must pass before VPN connection is established.

All third-party vendors with access to corporate data or systems must complete a security assessment before onboarding. Vendors handling Restricted or Confidential data must provide SOC 2 Type II reports annually. Vendor access must be reviewed quarterly and terminated within 24 hours of contract completion.

All data at rest classified as Confidential or Restricted must be encrypted using AES-256 or equivalent. All data in transit must use TLS 1.2 or higher. Encryption keys must be managed through the corporate key management system with annual rotation for data-at-rest keys.

Access to systems and data must follow the principle of least privilege. User access rights must be reviewed quarterly by data owners. Privileged access requires separate admin accounts with just-in-time provisioning and session recording. All access grants must be documented with business justification.

The incident response team must maintain and test the incident response plan at least annually through tabletop exercises and simulated incident drills. Post-incident reviews must be completed within 5 business days of incident closure, with lessons learned incorporated into updated runbooks.

Personal data of EU residents must be processed in accordance with GDPR requirements. Data processing activities must be documented in the Records of Processing Activities register. Data subject access requests must be fulfilled within 30 days. Data breach notification to supervisory authorities must occur within 72 hours.

Service accounts must use managed service account credentials where supported. Service account passwords must be at least 32 characters, randomly generated, and stored in the approved secrets management vault. Service accounts must not be used for interactive login and must be scoped to minimum required permissions.

Vulnerability scans must be conducted weekly for all internal systems and daily for internet-facing assets. Critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within 7 days, high within 30 days, medium within 90 days, and low within 180 days. Exceptions require CISO approval with documented compensating controls.

All employee workstations and servers must run approved endpoint detection and response software. EDR agents must not be disabled or tampered with. Endpoints failing compliance checks are automatically quarantined from the network until remediation is verified.

Cardholder data must be protected in accordance with PCI DSS v4.0 requirements. Credit card numbers must be masked in display, encrypted in storage, and transmitted only over encrypted channels. Access to cardholder data environments is restricted to personnel with documented business need.

Network segmentation must isolate production, development, and corporate environments. Database servers must not be directly accessible from user VLANs. All inter-VLAN traffic must traverse a firewall with explicit allow rules. Network architecture diagrams must be reviewed and updated quarterly.

All employees must complete annual security awareness training within 30 days of assignment. New hires must complete training within their first week. Phishing simulation exercises are conducted monthly with a target click rate below 5 percent. Employees who fail two consecutive simulations must complete remedial training.

Cloud infrastructure must be deployed using infrastructure-as-code templates reviewed by the security team. Cloud storage buckets must not be publicly accessible unless explicitly approved. Cloud security posture management tools must continuously monitor for misconfigurations and alert on policy violations.

Mobile devices accessing corporate email or data must be enrolled in the mobile device management platform. Device encryption must be enabled, screen lock must activate within 5 minutes, and remote wipe capability must be configured. Jailbroken or rooted devices are prohibited from accessing corporate resources.

Security event logs from all critical systems must be forwarded to the SIEM platform in real time. Log retention must be a minimum of 1 year for standard logs and 7 years for logs related to financial transactions or regulated data. Log integrity must be ensured through tamper-evident mechanisms.

Business continuity and disaster recovery plans must be maintained for all critical business processes. Recovery Time Objective for critical systems is 4 hours and Recovery Point Objective is 1 hour. DR plans must be tested semi-annually with documented results and improvement actions.

Software development must follow secure SDLC practices including threat modeling during design, static analysis during development, and dynamic testing before release. All code changes must be peer-reviewed. Dependencies must be scanned for known vulnerabilities before deployment to production.

Vendor risk assessments must be updated annually or when significant changes occur to the vendor relationship. Critical vendors must maintain cyber insurance with minimum coverage of 10 million USD. Vendor contracts must include right-to-audit clauses and data breach notification requirements.

Privileged access to production systems must be provisioned through the Privileged Access Management system with time-limited sessions. All privileged sessions must be recorded and available for audit review. Standing privileged access is prohibited; just-in-time access with approval workflow is required.

Data retention and disposal must follow the approved retention schedule. Electronic media containing Confidential or Restricted data must be sanitized using NIST SP 800-88 compliant methods before disposal. Certificates of destruction must be obtained from approved disposal vendors and retained for 3 years.

API endpoints must implement authentication using OAuth 2.0 or mutual TLS. Rate limiting must be enforced on all public APIs. API keys must be rotated every 90 days and must not be embedded in client-side code. API access logs must be retained for a minimum of 1 year.

Physical access to data centers and server rooms must be controlled via badge readers with biometric verification. Visitor access requires escort by authorized personnel at all times. Access logs must be reviewed monthly. Environmental controls including fire suppression, HVAC, and UPS must be tested quarterly.

A new policy framework for AI and machine learning system governance is under development. The draft covers requirements for model inventory, bias testing, data provenance, explainability, and security testing of ML pipelines. Alignment with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework is being evaluated.

All AI and machine learning systems deployed in production must be registered in the AI model inventory with documented purpose, training data sources, performance metrics, and risk classification. Models processing personal data require a Data Protection Impact Assessment. Generative AI tools must not be used with Confidential or Restricted data unless deployed through the approved enterprise AI platform with data protection agreements. AI outputs used in decision-making must include human review for high-impact decisions.

All cloud workloads must be deployed in approved cloud provider accounts managed by the Cloud Center of Excellence. Multi-cloud deployments must use the organization's cloud management platform for governance and cost control. Cloud resources must be tagged with owner, environment, data classification, and cost center. Internet-facing cloud resources require security review and approval before deployment. Cloud provider root and master account credentials must be protected with hardware MFA and restricted to break-glass procedures.

Container images must be built from approved base images maintained in the private registry. All images must pass vulnerability scanning before deployment with no critical or high findings. Container runtime must enforce read-only root filesystems, non-root user execution, and dropped capabilities. Kubernetes pod security standards at the restricted level must be enforced in production namespaces. Container images must be signed and signature verified at admission.

All APIs must be documented in the API catalog with OpenAPI specifications. APIs handling sensitive data must implement field-level encryption for PII in transit. API authentication tokens must have maximum lifetime of 1 hour for access tokens and 24 hours for refresh tokens. All API endpoints must implement input validation against their schema. GraphQL APIs must enforce query depth and complexity limits to prevent denial-of-service through nested queries.

IoT devices deployed on the corporate network must be inventoried and registered with the asset management system. IoT devices must be isolated in dedicated network segments with firewall rules restricting communication to only required endpoints and protocols. Default credentials must be changed before deployment. Firmware updates must be applied within 30 days of vendor release. IoT devices must not store corporate credentials or sensitive data locally.

Employees must not disclose Confidential or Restricted company information on social media platforms. Corporate social media accounts must use unique passwords managed through the secrets vault with MFA enabled. Employees must not list internal project names, code names, or technical infrastructure details on public profiles. Social media usage on corporate devices must comply with the acceptable use policy. Phishing or social engineering attacks conducted via social media must be reported to the SOC immediately.

Personal devices used for business purposes under the BYOD program must be enrolled in the mobile device management platform. BYOD devices must maintain a minimum OS version within two major releases of current. Corporate data must be stored in managed application containers with remote wipe capability limited to the corporate container. BYOD devices must have screen lock enabled with maximum 5-minute timeout, device encryption active, and no jailbreak or root detected. Employees must sign the BYOD agreement acknowledging IT inspection rights for the managed container.

Data retention schedules must be defined for all data categories and enforced through automated lifecycle policies. Financial records must be retained for 7 years. Employee records must be retained for 3 years post-separation. Customer transaction data must be retained for 5 years. Security logs must be retained for 1 year in hot storage and 7 years in archive. Data past its retention period must be securely deleted within 90 days of expiration unless subject to legal hold.

Security awareness training must include role-specific modules in addition to general awareness content. Developers must complete secure coding training annually. Finance personnel must complete BEC and wire fraud awareness training quarterly. Executives must complete targeted social engineering awareness training. IT administrators must complete privileged access security training. Training completion rates must be reported monthly to department heads with escalation for non-compliance.

All third-party and open-source code incorporated into production applications must undergo security review. Open-source components must be sourced from the approved private artifact registry. Components with known critical vulnerabilities must not be used unless a documented exception with compensating controls is approved by the CISO. Software Bill of Materials must be generated for all production deployments and retained for the lifetime of the application.

The secure software development lifecycle must be followed for all internally developed applications. Threat modeling is required during the design phase for all applications handling Confidential or Restricted data. Static application security testing must be integrated into CI/CD pipelines with build failure on critical findings. Dynamic application security testing must be performed before each production release. Penetration testing must be conducted annually for all customer-facing applications.

Incident communications must follow the documented communication protocol. Internal stakeholders must be notified within 1 hour of a confirmed critical or high severity incident. External communications including customer notifications, press statements, and regulatory filings must be approved by Legal and Communications before release. A designated incident spokesperson must handle all media inquiries. Status updates must be provided to stakeholders at minimum every 4 hours during active critical incidents.

Wireless networks must use WPA3-Enterprise with certificate-based 802.1X authentication for corporate SSIDs. Guest wireless networks must be isolated from corporate networks with bandwidth throttling and content filtering. Rogue access point detection must be enabled on all wireless infrastructure. Wireless network security assessments must be conducted semi-annually. Personal hotspots and unauthorized wireless access points are prohibited in corporate facilities.

Secrets management must use the approved enterprise vault solution. Hard-coded credentials in source code, configuration files, and container images are prohibited. Application secrets must be injected at runtime from the vault using service identity authentication. Secret rotation must occur every 90 days for API keys, every 365 days for encryption keys, and immediately upon suspected compromise. Pre-commit hooks for secret detection must be enabled on all repositories.

Email security controls must include SPF, DKIM, and DMARC with a policy of reject for the corporate domain. External emails must be tagged with a visual warning banner. Attachment sandboxing must be enabled for all inbound emails. URL rewriting and time-of-click analysis must be active. Users must not auto-forward corporate email to personal email accounts. Email DLP policies must inspect outbound messages for Confidential and Restricted data.

Cryptographic key management must follow NIST SP 800-57 guidelines. Hardware security modules must be used for root CA private keys and code signing keys. Key generation must use FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules. Key ceremonies for critical keys must require dual control with segregation of duties. Key compromise procedures must be documented and tested annually.

Supply chain security must be maintained through vendor security assessments, software composition analysis, and continuous monitoring of third-party risk. Critical software vendors must provide SBOMs with each release. Vendors with network access must comply with the same endpoint security standards as internal systems. Supply chain incidents must be treated as high-priority events with immediate triage and containment procedures.

Database security policy requires all production databases to enforce authentication, authorization, and encryption for connections. Database administrator access must be provisioned through the PAM system with session recording. Database activity monitoring must be enabled for all databases containing Confidential or Restricted data. Direct production database access by developers is prohibited; read-only replicas with anonymized data must be used for troubleshooting.

Threat intelligence operations must maintain subscriptions to commercial and open-source threat intelligence feeds relevant to the organization's industry and threat profile. IOCs from threat intelligence must be operationalized within 24 hours of receipt through automated feed integration with detection platforms. Threat intelligence must be shared with industry ISACs and trusted peer organizations in accordance with TLP marking guidelines.

Identity governance and administration must ensure that all user access is provisioned through the centralized identity management platform. Joiners, movers, and leavers processes must be automated with HR system integration. Access must be provisioned based on role definitions with separation of duties enforcement. Orphaned accounts must be detected and disabled within 7 days. Quarterly access certification campaigns must cover all applications processing Confidential or Restricted data.
